solution:
Integrate term by term using the power rule \(\int x^n\, dx = \dfrac{x^{n+1}}{n+1}\):
\(\int (x^3 + x^2 - x + 1)\, dx = \dfrac{x^4}{4} + \dfrac{x^3}{3} - \dfrac{x^2}{2} + x + c\)

First expand the integrand:
\(x^2\left(1 - \dfrac{2}{x}\right)^2 = x^2\left(1 - \dfrac{4}{x} + \dfrac{4}{x^2}\right) = x^2 - 4x + 4\).
\(\int (x^2 - 4x + 4)\, dx = \dfrac{x^3}{3} - 2x^2 + 4x + c\)

Write \(\dfrac{1}{x\sqrt{x}} = x^{-3/2}\).
\(\int\left(3\sec^2 x - \dfrac{4}{x} + x^{-3/2} - 7\right) dx = 3\tan x - 4\log|x| + \dfrac{x^{-1/2}}{-1/2} - 7x + c\)
\(= 3\tan x - 4\log|x| - \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{x}} - 7x + c\)

[Textbook answer-key error: the printed key's first term is \(\frac{x^2}{4}\); the correct first term is \(\int 2x^3\, dx = \frac{x^4}{2}\) (the exponent and denominator were swapped, \(4 \leftrightarrow 2\)). The answer below is correct.]

Write \(\dfrac{4}{x^5} = 4x^{-5}\) and integrate term by term:
\(\int\left(2x^3 - 5x + \dfrac{3}{x} + 4x^{-5}\right) dx = \dfrac{2x^4}{4} - \dfrac{5x^2}{2} + 3\log|x| + \dfrac{4x^{-4}}{-4} + c\)
\(= \dfrac{x^4}{2} - \dfrac{5x^2}{2} + 3\log|x| - \dfrac{1}{x^4} + c\)

Use \(\tan^2 x = \sec^2 x - 1\):
\(\int \tan^2 x\, dx = \int(\sec^2 x - 1)\, dx = \tan x - x + c\)

Use \(\sin 2x = 2\sin x\cos x\):
\(\int \dfrac{\sin 2x}{\cos x}\, dx = \int \dfrac{2\sin x\cos x}{\cos x}\, dx = \int 2\sin x\, dx = -2\cos x + c\)

Split the fraction:
\(\dfrac{\sin x}{\cos^2 x} = \dfrac{1}{\cos x}\cdot\dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x} = \sec x\tan x\).
\(\int \sec x\tan x\, dx = \sec x + c\)

Use \(\cos 2x = 1 - 2\sin^2 x\):
\(\dfrac{\cos 2x}{\sin^2 x} = \dfrac{1 - 2\sin^2 x}{\sin^2 x} = \csc^2 x - 2\).
\(\int(\csc^2 x - 2)\, dx = -\cot x - 2x + c\)

[Textbook answer-key error: the printed key adds a spurious \(+x\), giving \(-\cot x - \tan x + x\). Since the integrand is \(\csc^2 x - \sec^2 x\), the integral is \(-\cot x - \tan x + c\) with no linear term. The answer below is correct.]

Use \(\cos 2x = \cos^2 x - \sin^2 x\):
\(\dfrac{\cos^2 x - \sin^2 x}{\sin^2 x\cos^2 x} = \dfrac{1}{\sin^2 x} - \dfrac{1}{\cos^2 x} = \csc^2 x - \sec^2 x\).
\(\int(\csc^2 x - \sec^2 x)\, dx = -\cot x - \tan x + c\)

Write \(\dfrac{\sin x}{1+\sin x} = 1 - \dfrac{1}{1+\sin x}\). Rationalise the second term:
\(\dfrac{1}{1+\sin x}\cdot\dfrac{1-\sin x}{1-\sin x} = \dfrac{1-\sin x}{\cos^2 x} = \sec^2 x - \sec x\tan x\).
So the integrand \(= 1 - \sec^2 x + \sec x\tan x\).
\(\int(1 - \sec^2 x + \sec x\tan x)\, dx = x - \tan x + \sec x + c\)

Multiply numerator and denominator by \(\sec x - \tan x\). Since \((\sec x+\tan x)(\sec x-\tan x) = \sec^2 x - \tan^2 x = 1\):
\(\dfrac{\tan x}{\sec x+\tan x} = \tan x(\sec x - \tan x) = \sec x\tan x - \tan^2 x = \sec x\tan x - (\sec^2 x - 1)\).
\(\int(\sec x\tan x - \sec^2 x + 1)\, dx = \sec x - \tan x + x + c\)

Use \(1 + \sin 2x = \sin^2 x + \cos^2 x + 2\sin x\cos x = (\sin x + \cos x)^2\):
\(\sqrt{1+\sin 2x} = \sin x + \cos x\).
\(\int(\sin x + \cos x)\, dx = -\cos x + \sin x + c = \sin x - \cos x + c\)

Use \(1 - \cos 2x = 2\sin^2 x\):
\(\sqrt{1-\cos 2x} = \sqrt{2}\,|\sin x| = \sqrt{2}\,\sin x\).
\(\int \sqrt{2}\,\sin x\, dx = -\sqrt{2}\cos x + c\)

Use the product-to-sum formula \(\sin A\cos B = \dfrac{1}{2}[\sin(A+B) + \sin(A-B)]\):
\(\sin 4x\cos 3x = \dfrac{1}{2}(\sin 7x + \sin x)\).
\(\int \dfrac{1}{2}(\sin 7x + \sin x)\, dx = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(-\dfrac{\cos 7x}{7} - \cos x\right) + c = -\dfrac{\cos 7x}{14} - \dfrac{\cos x}{2} + c\)

Write \(\dfrac{x}{x+2} = \dfrac{(x+2)-2}{x+2} = 1 - \dfrac{2}{x+2}\).
\(\int\left(1 - \dfrac{2}{x+2}\right) dx = x - 2\log|x+2| + c\)

[Textbook answer-key error: the printed key gives \(-\frac{26}{9}\log|3x-4|\); the sign is wrong. From \(5x+2 = \frac{5}{3}(3x-4) + \frac{26}{3}\), the log coefficient is \(+\frac{26}{9}\). The answer below is correct.]

Write \(5x+2 = \dfrac{5}{3}(3x-4) + \dfrac{26}{3}\), so \(\dfrac{5x+2}{3x-4} = \dfrac{5}{3} + \dfrac{26}{3(3x-4)}\).
\(\int\left(\dfrac{5}{3} + \dfrac{26}{3(3x-4)}\right) dx = \dfrac{5}{3}x + \dfrac{26}{9}\log|3x-4| + c\)

Use \(\sin 4x = 2\sin 2x\cos 2x\):
\(\dfrac{\sin 4x}{\cos 2x} = \dfrac{2\sin 2x\cos 2x}{\cos 2x} = 2\sin 2x\).
\(\int 2\sin 2x\, dx = 2\cdot\dfrac{-\cos 2x}{2} + c = -\cos 2x + c\)

Use \(1 + \sin 5x = \left(\sin\dfrac{5x}{2} + \cos\dfrac{5x}{2}\right)^2\):
\(\sqrt{1+\sin 5x} = \sin\dfrac{5x}{2} + \cos\dfrac{5x}{2}\).
\(\int\left(\sin\dfrac{5x}{2} + \cos\dfrac{5x}{2}\right) dx = \dfrac{-\cos(5x/2)}{5/2} + \dfrac{\sin(5x/2)}{5/2} + c = \dfrac{2}{5}\left(\sin\dfrac{5x}{2} - \cos\dfrac{5x}{2}\right) + c\)

Use \(\cos^2 x = \dfrac{1+\cos 2x}{2}\):
\(\int \cos^2 x\, dx = \int \dfrac{1+\cos 2x}{2}\, dx = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(x + \dfrac{\sin 2x}{2}\right) + c = \dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{\sin 2x}{4} + c\)

Rationalise by multiplying numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{x+3}\):
\(\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{x}-\sqrt{x+3}}\cdot\dfrac{\sqrt{x}+\sqrt{x+3}}{\sqrt{x}+\sqrt{x+3}} = \dfrac{2(\sqrt{x}+\sqrt{x+3})}{x-(x+3)} = -\dfrac{2}{3}\left(\sqrt{x}+\sqrt{x+3}\right)\).
\(\int -\dfrac{2}{3}\left(x^{1/2}+(x+3)^{1/2}\right) dx = -\dfrac{2}{3}\left[\dfrac{2}{3}x^{3/2} + \dfrac{2}{3}(x+3)^{3/2}\right] + c\)
\(= -\dfrac{4}{9}\left[x^{3/2} + (x+3)^{3/2}\right] + c\)

Rationalise by multiplying numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{7x-2}+\sqrt{7x-5}\):
\(\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{7x-2}-\sqrt{7x-5}}\cdot\dfrac{\sqrt{7x-2}+\sqrt{7x-5}}{\sqrt{7x-2}+\sqrt{7x-5}} = \dfrac{3(\sqrt{7x-2}+\sqrt{7x-5})}{(7x-2)-(7x-5)} = \sqrt{7x-2}+\sqrt{7x-5}\).
\(\int\left[(7x-2)^{1/2}+(7x-5)^{1/2}\right] dx = \dfrac{1}{7}\cdot\dfrac{2}{3}(7x-2)^{3/2} + \dfrac{1}{7}\cdot\dfrac{2}{3}(7x-5)^{3/2} + c\)
\(= \dfrac{2}{21}\left[(7x-2)^{3/2}+(7x-5)^{3/2}\right] + c\)

Integrate \(f'(x)\) to recover \(f(x)\). Write \(\dfrac{3}{x^3} = 3x^{-3}\):
\(f(x) = \int\left(x - 3x^{-3}\right) dx = \dfrac{x^2}{2} - 3\cdot\dfrac{x^{-2}}{-2} + c = \dfrac{x^2}{2} + \dfrac{3}{2x^2} + c\).
Apply \(f(1) = \dfrac{11}{2}\): \(\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{3}{2} + c = \dfrac{11}{2}\), so \(2 + c = \dfrac{11}{2}\), giving \(c = \dfrac{7}{2}\).
Therefore \(f(x) = \dfrac{x^2}{2} + \dfrac{3}{2x^2} + \dfrac{7}{2}\).
